handoff.purpose: Define public functions for minting tasks from landed edits and commits, confirming tasks, and loading persisted minted tasks.

symbols.name: mint_task_from_landed_edit
symbols.note: Mints one quarantined task from a landed offload edit. Uses disk_changed from report['wrote'] to get actual changes. Reads before from git HEAD, after from worktree. Returns None if nothing to mint.

symbols.name: mint_from_commit
symbols.note: Mints quarantined task(s) from one real git commit. Uses git diff-tree to get changed files. Returns list of tasks (currently at most one) or [].

symbols.name: confirm_task
symbols.note: Records one independent confirmation of a minted task, promoting tier from quarantine to primary if threshold reached. Mutates the dict in place.

symbols.name: load_minted_tasks
symbols.note: Reads persisted mint store from JSON file. Returns sorted list of tasks by id, or [] if file doesn't exist.

claims.text: report["wrote"] IS disk_changed from offload.py:194-197 -- the files that ACTUALLY changed on disk, found by diffing a before/after content-hash snapshot taken around the run.
claims.why: The referenced file offload.py is not in this chunk; cannot verify the claim.

claims.text: The edit is assumed uncommitted (offload writes straight into the working tree and never commits): "before" is read from git HEAD, "after" from the file currently on disk.
claims.why: The code shows: before = _show(repo_root, 'HEAD', rel) if sha else None; after = _read_worktree(repo_root, rel). This matches the claim.

claims.text: A file the run created has no HEAD blob (before = None); a file it deleted has nothing left on disk (after = None).
claims.why: The code sets before = _show(...) which returns None if the file does not exist in HEAD; after = _read_worktree(...) returns None if file does not exist on disk. So the claim holds.

claims.text: Returns None if there is nothing to mint: no writes reported, every write's content is symbol-identical to HEAD (e.g. a formatting-only touch this diff granularity can't see through), no written file is in the project's index scope, or only one in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists -- see the module docstring's CROSS-FILE ONLY rule).
claims.why: The function returns None if disk_changed is empty (no writes) but the other conditions (content identical, scope, cross-file label) depend on _mint_from_diffs which is not in this chunk. Cannot verify.

claims.text: Same idea as mint_task_from_landed_edit, but against history that already exists -- this is what lets minting be exercised deterministically in tests without a live offload run (a temp git fixture IS real git history; git show gives exact before/after text with no mocking).
claims.why: The claim about testing and mocking is not verifiable from this code chunk. The function does use _show (which runs git show) and git diff-tree, so the mechanism is present, but the testing context is outside.

claims.text: Currently mints a single aggregate task per commit (via the same _mint_from_diffs used for landed edits); returns a list so a future split (e.g. one task per hunk, for very large commits) is additive rather than a signature change.
claims.why: The code calls _mint_from_diffs and then returns [task] if task else []. That returns a list with at most one element, matching the claim.

claims.text: Returns [] for an unresolvable ref, a commit that touches no in-scope file, or one where only a single in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists) -- never raises.
claims.why: The code returns [] if full_sha is None (unresolvable ref) or if name_status is None. But the other conditions (no in-scope file, single file) depend on _mint_from_diffs which is not in this chunk. Cannot verify fully.

claims.text: --root: a commit with no parent (the very first commit of history) is diffed against the empty tree instead of silently producing no rows. No-op for every other commit (it already has a parent to diff against).
claims.why: The code uses '--root' in the git diff-tree command, which causes root commits to be compared to the empty tree. This matches the claim.

claims.text: Promotes task["tier"] from "quarantine" to "primary" once confirmations reaches MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD.
claims.why: The code checks if task['confirmations'] >= MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD and sets task['tier'] = 'primary'. This matches the claim.

claims.text: A no-op on a task that is not currently quarantined: a primary task doesn't need more confirming, and "confirming" a hand_reachable task is meaningless -- it was never gated in the first place.
claims.why: The code returns early if task.get('tier') != 'quarantine'. This matches the claim.

claims.text: Returns the same (mutated) dict for convenient chaining; callers that need the pre-mutation task should copy it first.
claims.why: The function returns the same dict object (task) after mutation. This matches the claim.

claims.text: This is the ONLY load path by which a minted task can reach daedalus.eval.harness.all_tasks() and therefore any go/no-go number -- without it, mint_task_from_landed_edit/mint_from_commit produced dicts that lived only as long as the caller's local variable.
claims.why: The referenced module daedalus.eval.harness is not in this chunk; cannot verify the claim about being the only load path.

claims.text: Sorted by id for deterministic iteration (PYTHONHASHSEED-independent), matching the rest of this repo's output-determinism rule.
claims.why: The code returns sorted(data.get('tasks', []), key=lambda t: t['id']). This sorts by id, which is deterministic. The claim about PYTHONHASHSEED independence is implied but sorting by id is indeed independent of hash seed.

observations.what: mint_task_from_landed_edit uses _resolve_sha and _show with 'HEAD' but does not handle the case where sha resolves but the commit does not contain the file; _show may return None as expected.
mint_from_commit uses --root flag to handle root commits; parent is None for root commits, and _show with None parent returns None for before.
confirm_task increments confirmations even if the task dict has no 'confirmations' key, using int(task.get('confirmations', 0)).
load_minted_tasks returns [] if path does not exist; otherwise it reads JSON and returns sorted tasks. The path defaults to DEFAULT_MINT_STORE_PATH which is not defined in this chunk.
